facts.statement: Indosuchus lived in India during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Maastrichtian age, between approximately 70 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Indosuchus () is an extinct genus of abelisaurid theropod from the Late Cretaceous of India, approximately 70–66 million years ago, during the Maastrichtian age.

facts.statement: Indosuchus reached a length of approximately 7 meters and an estimated weight of 1.2 tons.
facts.quote: It measured approximately 7 m in length and weighed and estimated 1.2 t.

facts.statement: The skull of Indosuchus was flattened across the top and featured a prominent crest.
facts.quote: Its skull was flattened across the top and bore a prominent crest.

facts.statement: Indosuchus was named by Friedrich von Huene in 1932 and formally described by Huene and Charles Alfred Matley in 1933.
facts.quote: Indosuchus was named by Friedrich von Huene in 1932 and formally described by Huene and Charles Alfred Matley in 1933.

facts.statement: The original description of Indosuchus was based on three partial skulls found near Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh, India, within the Lameta Formation.
facts.quote: The description was based on three partial skulls discovered by Matley near Jabalpur, in Madhya Pradesh within the Lameta Formation.

facts.statement: The known remains of the lectotype specimen have been lost since its description.
facts.quote: The known remains of the lectotype have since been lost.

facts.statement: The genus name Indosuchus combines the Ancient Greek name for the Indus River and the Greek name for the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
facts.quote: The generic name Indosuchus combines Indos, the Ancient Greek name for the Indus River, and Soukhos, the Greek name for the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.

facts.statement: Indosuchus is now firmly classified within the Abelisauridae, though it was originally assigned to the Allosauridae by von Huene.
facts.quote: Although it is now somewhat firmly placed within the Abelisauridae, it was originally assigned by von Huene to the Allosauridae.

facts.statement: In 1964, Alick Walker hypothesized that Indosuchus was a member of the Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Alick Walker thought in 1964 it was a member of the Tyrannosauridae.

facts.statement: In 1986, José Bonaparte concluded that Indosuchus was an abelisaurid.
facts.quote: in 1986 José Bonaparte concluded it was an abelisaurid.

facts.statement: According to Novas et al. in 2004, Indosuchus is defined by the anterior placement of the frontonasal suture relative to the lacrimal bone.
facts.quote: Indosuchus is defined based on how the frontonasal suture is placed anteriorly compared to lacrimal, according to Novas et al., 2004.

facts.statement: Indosuchus was a medium-sized theropod measuring about 7 meters in length, 2.2 meters in height, and weighing 1,200 kilograms.
facts.quote: Indosuchus era un terópodo de tamaño mediano de unos 7 metros de longitud y 2,2 de altura con un peso de 1200 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Indosuchus had tiny arms and small crests above its eyes similar to those of Allosaurus, which were smaller than those of other abelisaurids.
facts.quote: Tenía brazos diminutos, en la cabeza tenía protuberancias pero de menor tamaño que otros abelisáuridos, unas crestas pequeñas encima de los ojos parecidas a las del Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Additional cranial and postcranial material, including an almost complete skeleton from the Raiholi site in Gujarat, has been referred to I. raptorius by Walker in 1964, Chatterjee in 1978, and a nearly complete skeleton in 1995.
facts.quote: Más material craneal y postcraneal ha sido referido a I. raptorius por Walker en 1964 y Chatterjee en 1978, además de un esqueleto casi completo 1995, del sitio de Raiholi en Gujrat.

facts.statement: Because only some skull elements have been found, the classification of Indosuchus has been somewhat erratic.
facts.quote: Debido a que solo se han encontrado algunos elementos del cráneo, la colocación de Indosuchus ha sido algo errática.

facts.statement: The time range for Indosuchus is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
